title: Duplin County holiday celebrations in full swing with parades, festivals and community traditions - NewsBreak
text:
By Christopher DeWitt ,
1 days ago
The holidays are here. Hopefully you have gotten a jumpstart on your shopping and are enjoying some seasonal sweets. Celebrations are getting underway in Duplin County. Events such as holiday parades and Christmas tree lightings are available for your family to enjoy.
Here are some of the upcoming festivities you can add to your calendar.
Rose Hill Christmas by the Tracks
Saturday, Dec. 6
Rose Hill’s holiday festival continues to evolve and expand. Now in its third year, the event blends crafters, local performers and a night parade that will make for a full day the whole family can enjoy.
“As of right now, we have quite a few participants in this year’s celebration,” said Rose Hill Christmas by the Tracks Chairperson Ronda Rivenbark. “We have reached out to businesses, schools (and) different organizations. In past years, the festival has battled rain and bitter cold, but turnout has remained enthusiastic.”
Christmas by the Tracks kicks off at noon Dec. 6 with a craft fair, which will have local artisans, homemade goods and food trucks. The celebration continues with the first half of entertainment at 4 p.m. Adam Quinn, Renee Hoxie, Vessel of Worship, Trinity Preschool and others will perform at this time.
The day will wrap up with the Night Parade at 6 p.m., with lineup happening at 5 p.m. on First Street. The parade’s grand marshal, Harvey Dalton Arnold, will take the stage with The Johnson Boys to cap off the day. Arnold is an N.C. native who has had a music career spanning over 50 years and was a member of '70s southern rock band The Outlaws.
A newly donated Christmas tree will be lit in honor of Rose Hill’s 150th anniversary, a milestone the town will continue celebrating throughout 2025.
“This event is totally done by volunteers,” Rivenbark said. “We are getting so excited! (We are) pleased with the amount of crafters, parade participants and the lineup for our entertainment. It’s just going to be a great day. I pray everyone walks away with the full Christmas spirit in their souls.”
Call Rivenbark at 910-289-1346 to learn more about Christmas by the Tracks and get parade entry information.
Goldsboro Christmas Parade
Saturday, Dec. 6
The annual Goldsboro Christmas Parade remains one of the area’s largest holiday events, and this year’s parade will feature a lively lineup of marching bands, a trackless train and members of the armed forces from Seymour Johnson Air Force Base.
“We are expecting over 100 participating organizations and more than 20,000 spectators for this year’s parade,” said Wayne County Chamber of Commerce Director of Events and Marketing Kaycee Johnson.
The parade will begin at 4 p.m. in downtown Goldsboro, starting at Chestnut Street and proceeding north on Center Street to Ash Street, then coming back down to end at Chestnut Street. Center Street will be closed starting at 1 p.m. Johnson urges spectators to plan accordingly for parking.
“Santa is a top draw, of course,” Johnson said. “But truly, there are too many highlights to choose from. We love all our participants.”
For more information, visit waynecountychamber.com/goldsborochristmasparade.
Additional holiday events in Duplin County
Here is a roundup of other holiday events happening in the area.
Wallace Christmas at Twilight: Saturday, Nov. 22
The Wallace Chamber of Commerce will present this annual evening of holiday celebration at the Wallace Train Depot. The festivities start at 4 p.m. and end at 8 p.m. The event will feature holiday carolers and other live performances, an antique car show, a hayride and a Christmas tree lighting to conclude the night. For more information, call Lisa Fussell at 910-284-6455.
Kenansville Christmas Parade: Saturday, Nov. 29
The Town of Kenansville and Kenansville Area Chamber of Commerce will host the Christmas Parade in downtown Kenansville. The parade will start at 11 a.m. For parade applications and more information, call the Kenansville Area Chamber of Commerce at 910-275-0323 or email kenansvillechamber@gmail.com.
Kenansville Tree Lighting
The Kenansville Christmas Tree Lighting will be held from 5-8 p.m. Nov. 30 at Kenan Park. The event will include photos with Santa, carol singing, letters to Santa and a Christmas movie. The tree lighting will take place at 6 p.m. Visit kenansville.org.
Warsaw tree lighting
The Town of Warsaw and Warsaw Chamber of Commerce will host a Christmas tree lighting at 6 p.m. Dec. 5 at Dreamworks Fitness Center on Hill Street. The event will include Christmas carols, hot chocolate and cookies and a visit from Santa.
Rose Hill
Rose Hill is seeking parade entries for the third annual “Christmas by the Tracks,” scheduled for 6 p.m. Dec. 6. There is no entry fee. Individuals, clubs and businesses are invited to participate in vehicles (of any kind) as well as homemade floats. Text Ronda Rivenbark at 910 289-1346.
